weapons.name: Javelin
weapons.description: A light spear designed for throwing.

weapons.name: Light Hammer
weapons.description: A small hammer, useful as a thrown weapon.

weapons.name: Mace
weapons.description: A metal rod with a heavy head, favoured by clerics.

weapons.name: Quarterstaff
weapons.description: A long wooden staff. Versatile: 1d8 two-handed.

weapons.name: Sickle
weapons.description: A short curved blade, used in harvesting.

weapons.name: Spear
weapons.description: A pole weapon with a metal tip. Versatile: 1d8 two-handed.

weapons.name: Light Crossbow
weapons.description: A mechanically drawn crossbow. Requires a bolt and one action to reload.

weapons.name: Dart
weapons.description: A small pointed projectile.

weapons.name: Shortbow
weapons.description: A small bow. Requires arrows.

weapons.name: Sling
weapons.description: A leather strap used to hurl stones or bullets.

weapons.name: Battleaxe
weapons.description: A single-headed axe. Versatile: 1d10 two-handed.

weapons.name: Flail
weapons.description: A spiked ball on a chain.

weapons.name: Glaive
weapons.description: A blade on a long pole. Reach: attack creatures 10 ft away.

weapons.name: Greataxe
weapons.description: A massive two-handed axe.

weapons.name: Greatsword
weapons.description: A massive two-handed sword.

weapons.name: Halberd
weapons.description: An axe-blade on a long pole with a spike on top.

weapons.name: Lance
weapons.description: Disadvantage on attacks within 5 ft. Requires one hand while mounted.

weapons.name: Longsword
weapons.description: A standard sword. Versatile: 1d10 two-handed.

weapons.name: Maul
weapons.description: A massive two-handed hammer.

weapons.name: Morningstar
weapons.description: A spiked metal ball on a handle.

weapons.name: Pike
weapons.description: A long pole weapon. Reach: attack creatures 10 ft away.

weapons.name: Rapier
weapons.description: A thin thrusting blade favoured by duelists.

weapons.name: Scimitar
weapons.description: A curved blade. Light, so usable for two-weapon fighting.

weapons.name: Shortsword
weapons.description: A short blade. Light and finesse, popular with rogues.

weapons.name: Trident
weapons.description: A three-pronged spear. Versatile: 1d8 two-handed.

weapons.name: War Pick
weapons.description: A pick designed for punching through armour.

weapons.name: Warhammer
weapons.description: A hammer designed for war. Versatile: 1d10 two-handed.

weapons.name: Whip
weapons.description: Reach: attack creatures up to 10 ft away.

weapons.name: Hand Crossbow
weapons.description: A one-handed crossbow.

weapons.name: Heavy Crossbow
weapons.description: A large, powerful crossbow.

weapons.name: Longbow
weapons.description: A large bow. Requires arrows and Str 15 to fire without disadvantage.

weapons.name: Net
weapons.description: Large or smaller creature: DC 10 Str save or restrained. No damage.

gear.name: Bagpipes
gear.description: A wind instrument with drone pipes.

gear.name: Drum
gear.description: A percussion instrument.

gear.name: Dulcimer
gear.description: A stringed instrument struck with hammers.

gear.name: Flute
gear.description: A small wind instrument.

gear.name: Lute
gear.description: A plucked stringed instrument.

gear.name: Lyre
gear.description: A small harp-like instrument.

gear.name: Horn
gear.description: A brass wind instrument.

gear.name: Pan Flute
gear.description: Multiple pipes of graduated length.

gear.name: Shawm
gear.description: A loud double-reed instrument.

gear.name: Viol
gear.description: A bowed stringed instrument.

gear.name: Crystal
gear.description: An arcane focus in the form of a crystal orb.

gear.name: Orb
gear.description: A glass or crystal sphere used as an arcane focus.

gear.name: Rod
gear.description: A metal rod etched with arcane sigils.

gear.name: Staff (focus)
gear.description: A wooden or metal staff used as an arcane focus.

gear.name: Wand
gear.description: A slender rod of wood or metal, carved with arcane runes.

gear.name: Sprig of Mistletoe
gear.description: A druidic focus of a sprig of mistletoe.

gear.name: Totem
gear.description: An animal fetish used as a druidic focus.

gear.name: Wooden Staff
gear.description: A staff carved from a living tree.

gear.name: Yew Wand
gear.description: A wand fashioned from yew wood.

gear.name: Amulet (holy symbol)
gear.description: A holy symbol worn as an amulet.

gear.name: Emblem (holy symbol)
gear.description: A holy symbol embossed on a shield or cloak.

gear.name: Reliquary
gear.description: A reliquary box containing a holy relic.

gear.name: Alchemist's Supplies
gear.description: Used to brew potions and work with chemicals.

gear.name: Brewer's Supplies
gear.description: Equipment for brewing ales and meads.

gear.name: Calligrapher's Supplies
gear.description: Inks, quills, and parchment for fine writing.

gear.name: Carpenter's Tools
gear.description: Tools for woodworking.

gear.name: Cartographer's Tools
gear.description: Tools for drawing and reading maps.

gear.name: Cobbler's Tools
gear.description: Tools for making and repairing footwear.

gear.name: Cook's Utensils
gear.description: Pots, knives, and utensils for cooking.

gear.name: Glassblower's Tools
gear.description: Tools for shaping molten glass.

gear.name: Jeweler's Tools
gear.description: Delicate tools for working with gems and metals.

gear.name: Leatherworker's Tools
gear.description: Tools for tanning and shaping leather.

gear.name: Mason's Tools
gear.description: Hammers, chisels, and levels for stonework.

gear.name: Painter's Supplies
gear.description: Brushes, palettes, and pigments.

gear.name: Potter's Tools
gear.description: Tools for shaping clay vessels.

gear.name: Smith's Tools
gear.description: Hammer, tongs, and files for metalwork.

gear.name: Tinker's Tools
gear.description: Fine tools for constructing and repairing small mechanical devices.

gear.name: Weaver's Tools
gear.description: Needles, thread, and looms for weaving.

gear.name: Woodcarver's Tools
gear.description: Knives and gouges for carving wood.

gear.name: Dice Set
gear.description: A set of polyhedral dice for games of chance.

gear.name: Dragonchess Set
gear.description: A complex strategy game played on a three-level board.

gear.name: Playing Card Set
gear.description: A deck of illustrated cards for games.

gear.name: Three-Dragon Ante Set
gear.description: Cards for a popular gambling game.

gear.name: Disguise Kit
gear.description: Cosmetics, hair dye, small props, and a few pieces of costume clothing. Proficiency allows you to change your appearance.

gear.name: Forgery Kit
gear.description: Various papers and parchments, as well as pens, inks, seals, and wax for creating convincing forgeries.

gear.name: Herbalism Kit
gear.description: Pouches and vials for collecting and identifying plants, plus tools for preparing remedies.

gear.name: Navigator's Tools
gear.description: Sextant, compass, calipers, ruler, parchment, ink, and quill for seafaring navigation.

gear.name: Poisoner's Kit
gear.description: Vials, chemicals, and a special syringe for creating poisons.

gear.name: Thieves' Tools
gear.description: Small file, set of lock picks, small mirror on a metal handle, narrow-bladed scissors, and a pair of pliers.

armor.name: Padded Armor
armor.description: Quilted layers of cloth and batting.

armor.name: Leather Armor
armor.description: The breastplate and shoulder protectors are made of leather that has been stiffened by being boiled in oil.

armor.name: Studded Leather
armor.description: Made from tough but flexible leather, studded with close-set rivets or spikes.

armor.name: Hide Armor
armor.description: This crude armor consists of thick furs and pelts.

armor.name: Chain Shirt
armor.description: Made of interlocking metal rings, a chain shirt is worn between layers of clothing or leather.

armor.name: Scale Mail
armor.description: This armor consists of a coat and leggings (and perhaps a separate skirt) of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish.

armor.name: Breastplate
armor.description: This armor consists of a fitted metal chest piece worn with supple leather. Although it leaves the legs and arms relatively unprotected, this armor provides good protection for the wearer's vital organs.

armor.name: Half Plate
armor.description: Half plate consists of shaped metal plates that cover most of the wearer's body. It does not include leg protection beyond simple greaves attached with leather straps.

armor.name: Ring Mail
armor.description: This armor is leather armor with heavy rings sewn into it. The rings help reinforce the armor against blows from swords and axes.

armor.name: Chain Mail
armor.description: Made of interlocking metal rings, chain mail includes a layer of quilted fabric worn underneath the mail to prevent chafing and to cushion the impact of blows.

armor.name: Splint Armor
armor.description: This armor is made of narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a backing of leather that is worn over cloth padding. Flexible chain mail protects the joints.

armor.name: Plate Armor
armor.description: Plate consists of shaped, interlocking metal plates to cover the entire body. A suit of plate includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, a visored helmet, and thick layers of padding underneath the armor.

armor.name: Shield
armor.description: A shield is made from wood or metal and is carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2.

armor.name: Wooden Shield
armor.description: A lightweight shield made from wood.

feats.name: Actor
feats.description: Skilled at mimicry and dramatics, you gain the following benefits: Increase CHA by 1 (max 20). You have advantage on Deception and Performance checks when trying to pass yourself off as a different person. You can mimic the speech of another person or the sounds made by other creatures.

feats.name: Alert
feats.description: Always on the lookout for danger, you gain the following benefits: +5 to initiative, you can't be surprised while conscious, other creatures don't gain advantage on attack rolls against you as a result of being hidden from you.

feats.name: Artificer Initiate
feats.description: You've learned some of an artificer's inventiveness. You gain the following benefits: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the artificer spell list, and you learn one 1st-level spell of your choice from that list. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells. You can cast this feat's 1st-level spell without a spell slot, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. You gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice, and you can use that type of tool as a spellcasting focus for any spell you cast that uses Intelligence as its spellcasting ability.

feats.name: Athlete
feats.description: You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits: Increase STR or DEX by 1 (max 20). When you are prone, standing up uses only 5 feet of movement. Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement. When you make a running long jump or running high jump, your speed must be at least 5 feet.

feats.name: Charger
feats.description: When you use your action to Dash, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to shove a creature. If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack's damage roll or push the target up to 10 feet if you choose to shove.

feats.name: Chef
feats.description: Time spent mastering the culinary arts has paid off. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Constitution or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with cook's utensils if you don't already have it. As part of a short rest, you can cook special food, provided you have ingredients and cook's utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 + your proficiency bonus. Each creature that eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice during the short rest can forgo one die roll and instead regain the maximum number of hit points the die can restore. With one hour of work or when you finish a long rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your proficiency bonus.

feats.name: Crossbow Expert
feats.description: Thanks to extensive practice with the crossbow, you ignore the loading quality of crossbows with which you are proficient. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls. When you use the Attack action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a hand crossbow.

feats.name: Crusher
feats.description: You are practiced in the art of crushing your enemies, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals bludgeoning damage, you can move it 5 feet to an unoccupied space, provided the target is no more than one size larger than you. When you score a critical hit that deals bludgeoning damage to a creature, attack rolls against that creature are made with advantage until the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Defensive Duelist
feats.description: When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack.

feats.name: Dragon Fear
feats.description: When angered, you radiate menace. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Instead of exhaling destructive energy, you can expend a use of your Breath Weapon trait to roar, forcing each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier). A target automatically succeeds if it can't hear or see you. On a failed save, a target becomes frightened of you for 1 minute. If the frightened target takes any damage, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

feats.name: Dragon Hide
feats.description: You manifest scales and claws reminiscent of your draconic ancestors. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength, Constitution, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Your scales harden. While you aren't wearing armor, you can calculate your AC as 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit. You grow retractable claws from the tips of your fingers. Extending or retracting the claws requires no action. The claws are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. If you hit with them, you deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your Strength modifier, instead of the normal bludgeoning damage for an unarmed strike.

feats.name: Drow High Magic
feats.description: You learn more of the magic typical of dark elves. You learn the detect magic spell and can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot. You also learn levitate and dispel magic, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast those two spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for all three spells.

feats.name: Dual Wielder
feats.description: You master fighting with two weapons, gaining the following benefits: +1 bonus to AC while you are wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand. You can use two-weapon fighting even when the one-handed melee weapons you are wielding aren't light. You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.

feats.name: Dungeon Delver
feats.description: Alert to the hidden traps and secret doors found in many dungeons, you gain the following benefits: Advantage on Perception and Investigation checks to detect secret doors. Advantage on saving throws to avoid or resist traps. Resistance to the damage dealt by traps. You can search for traps while traveling at a normal pace.

feats.name: Durable
feats.description: Hardy and resilient, you gain the following benefits: Increase CON by 1 (max 20). When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, the minimum number of hit points you regain is equal to twice your Constitution modifier.

feats.name: Eldritch Adept
feats.description: Studying occult lore, you have unlocked eldritch power within yourself. You learn one Eldritch Invocation option of your choice from the warlock class. If the invocation has a prerequisite of any kind, you can choose that invocation only if you're a warlock who meets the prerequisite. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace the invocation you chose with a new one from the warlock class.

feats.name: Elemental Adept
feats.description: When you gain this feat, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. When you roll damage for a spell of the chosen type and roll a 1, treat the die as if it had rolled a 2.

feats.name: Elven Accuracy
feats.description: The accuracy of elves is legendary, especially that of elf archers and spellcasters. You have uncanny aim with attacks that rely on precision rather than brute force. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Whenever you have advantage on an attack roll using Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can reroll one of the dice once.

feats.name: Fade Away
feats.description: Your people are clever, with a knack for illusion magic. You have learned a magical trick for fading away when you suffer harm. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity or Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Immediately after you take damage, you can use a reaction to magically become invisible until the end of your next turn or until you attack, deal damage, or force someone to make a saving throw. Once you use this ability, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

feats.name: Fey Teleportation
feats.description: Your study of high elven lore has unlocked fey power that few other elves possess, except your eladrin cousins. Drawing on your fey ancestry, you can momentarily stride through the Feywild to shorten your path from one place to another. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan. You learn the misty step spell and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a short or long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

feats.name: Fey Touched
feats.description: Your exposure to the Feywild's magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the misty step spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the divination or enchantment school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

feats.name: Fighting Initiate
feats.description: Your martial training has helped you develop a particular style of fighting. As a result, you learn one Fighting Style option of your choice from the fighter class. If you already have a style, the one you choose must be different. Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace this feat's fighting style with another one from the fighter class that you don't have.

feats.name: Flames of Phlegethos
feats.description: You learn to call on hellfire to serve your commands. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. When you roll fire damage for a spell you cast, you can reroll any roll of 1 on the fire damage dice, but you must use the new roll, even if it is another 1. Whenever you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can cause flames to wreathe you until the end of your next turn. The flames don't harm you or your possessions, and they shed bright light out to 30 feet and dim light out to an additional 30 feet. While the flames are present, any creature within 5 feet of you that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d4 fire damage.

feats.name: Grappler
feats.description: You've developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close-quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits: You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature you are grappling. You can use your action to try to pin a creature grappled by you.

feats.name: Great Weapon Master
feats.description: You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage: Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage. When you score a critical hit or reduce a creature to 0 HP with a melee weapon, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action.

feats.name: Gunner
feats.description: You have a quick hand and keen eye when employing firearms, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with firearms. You ignore the loading property of firearms. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

feats.name: Healer
feats.description: You are an able physician, allowing you to do the following: When you use a healer's kit to stabilise a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 HP. As an action, you can spend one use of a healer's kit to tend to a creature and restore 1d6 + 4 HP to it, plus additional HP equal to the creature's maximum number of Hit Dice.

feats.name: Heavily Armored
feats.description: You have trained to master the use of heavy armor, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

feats.name: Heavy Armor Master
feats.description: You can use your armor to deflect strikes that would kill others. Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20. While you are wearing heavy armor, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical weapons is reduced by 3.

feats.name: Infernal Constitution
feats.description: Fiendish blood runs strong in you, unlocking a resilience akin to that possessed by some fiends. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You have resistance to cold damage and poison damage. You have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.

feats.name: Inspiring Leader
feats.description: You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. Choose up to 6 friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet. Each creature can gain temporary HP equal to your level + your Charisma modifier.

feats.name: Keen Mind
feats.description: You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision. You gain the following benefits: Increase INT by 1 (max 20). You always know which way is north. You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset. You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

feats.name: Lightly Armored
feats.description: You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits: Increase STR or DEX by 1 (max 20). You gain proficiency with light armor.

feats.name: Linguist
feats.description: You have studied languages and codes, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn three languages of your choice. You can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.

feats.name: Lucky
feats.description: You have inexplicable luck that seems to kick in at just the right moment. You have 3 luck points. Whenever you make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can spend one luck point to roll an additional d20. You choose which die to use. You can also spend a luck point when an attack roll is made against you. Luck points are restored when you finish a long rest.

feats.name: Mage Slayer
feats.description: You have practiced techniques useful in melee combat against spellcasters, gaining the following benefits: When a creature within 5 feet of you casts a spell, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature. When you damage a creature that is concentrating on a spell, the creature has disadvantage on its saving throw. You have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creatures within 5 feet of you.

feats.name: Magic Initiate
feats.description: Choose a class: bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard. You learn two cantrips of your choice from that class's spell list. In addition, choose one 1st-level spell from that class's list. You learn that spell and can cast it once per long rest using this feat.

feats.name: Martial Adept
feats.description: You have martial training that allows you to perform special combat manoeuvres. You gain one superiority die (d6). You learn two manoeuvres of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype.

feats.name: Medium Armor Master
feats.description: You have practiced moving in medium armor to gain the following benefits: Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. When you wear medium armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.

feats.name: Metamagic Adept
feats.description: You've learned how to exert your will on your spells to alter how they function. You gain the following benefits: You learn two Metamagic options of your choice from the sorcerer class. You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless the option says otherwise. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with another one from the sorcerer class. You gain 2 sorcery points to spend on Metamagic (these points are added to any sorcery points you have from the Sorcerer class; the details on using sorcery points with Metamagic appear in the Sorcerer section).

feats.name: Mobile
feats.description: You are exceptionally speedy and agile. Your speed increases by 10 feet. When you use the Dash action, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement on that turn. When you make a melee attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn.

feats.name: Moderately Armored
feats.description: You have trained to master the use of medium armor and shields, gaining the following benefits: Increase STR or DEX by 1 (max 20). You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.

feats.name: Mounted Combatant
feats.description: You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted. While you are mounted and aren't incapacitated: You have advantage on melee attack rolls against unmounted creatures smaller than your mount. You can force an attack targeting your mount to target you instead. If your mount is subjected to an effect allowing a Dexterity saving throw for half damage, it takes no damage on a success.

feats.name: Observant
feats.description: Quick to notice details of your environment, you gain the following benefits: Increase INT or WIS by 1 (max 20). If you can see a creature's mouth while it is speaking a language you understand, you can interpret what it's saying by reading its lips. +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores.

feats.name: Orcish Fury
feats.description: Your fury burns tirelessly. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. When you hit with an attack using a simple or martial weapon, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice an additional time and add it as extra damage of the weapon's damage type. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest. Immediately after you use your Relentless Endurance trait, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack.

feats.name: Piercer
feats.description: You have achieved a penetrating precision in combat, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals piercing damage, you can reroll one of the attack's damage dice, and you must use the new roll. When you score a critical hit that deals piercing damage to a creature, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the extra piercing damage the target takes.

feats.name: Poisoner
feats.description: You can prepare and deliver deadly poisons, granting you the following benefits: When you make a damage roll that deals poison damage, it ignores resistance to poison damage. You can apply poison to a weapon or piece of ammunition as a bonus action, instead of an action. You gain proficiency with the poisoner's kit if you don't already have it. With one hour of work using a poisoner's kit and expending 50 gp worth of materials, you can create a number of doses of potent poison equal to your proficiency bonus.

feats.name: Polearm Master
feats.description: You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons. When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, or quarterstaff, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon (1d4 bludgeoning). While wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, or quarterstaff, other creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you when they enter your reach.

feats.name: Prodigy
feats.description: You have a knack for learning new things. You gain the following benefits: You gain one skill proficiency of your choice, one tool proficiency of your choice, and fluency in one language of your choice. Choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. The skill you choose must be one that isn't already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.

feats.name: Resilient
feats.description: Choose one ability score. You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability, and that ability score increases by 1 (max 20).

feats.name: Ritual Caster
feats.description: You have learned a number of spells that you can cast as rituals. Choose one class: bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard. You learn two 1st-level spells that have the ritual tag from that class's spell list.

feats.name: Savage Attacker
feats.description: Once per turn when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.

feats.name: Second Chance
feats.description: Fortune favors you when someone tries to strike you. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Dexterity, Constitution, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force that creature to reroll. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you roll initiative at the start of combat or until you finish a short or long rest.

feats.name: Sentinel
feats.description: You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard. When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, its speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn. Creatures within 5 feet of you provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action. When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack.

feats.name: Shadow Touched
feats.description: Your exposure to the Shadowfell's magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the invisibility spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the illusion or necromancy school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells' spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

feats.name: Sharpshooter
feats.description: You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots others find impossible. Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage. Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover. Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

feats.name: Shield Master
feats.description: You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to shove a creature within 5 feet. If you aren't incapacitated, you can add your shield's AC bonus to Dexterity saving throws. If you are subjected to an effect allowing a Dex save for half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage on a success.

feats.name: Skill Expert
feats.description: You have honed your proficiency with particular skills, granting you the following benefits: Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice. Choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. The skill you choose must be one that isn't already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.

feats.name: Skilled
feats.description: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

feats.name: Skulker
feats.description: You are expert at slinking through shadows. You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding. When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position. Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight.

feats.name: Slasher
feats.description: You've learned where to cut to have the greatest results, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals slashing damage, you can reduce the speed of the target by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. When you score a critical hit that deals slashing damage to a creature, you grievously wound it. Until the start of your next turn, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls.

feats.name: Spell Sniper
feats.description: You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits: When you cast a spell that requires an attack roll, the spell's range is doubled. Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover. You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll.

feats.name: Squat Nimbleness
feats.description: You are uncommonly nimble for your race. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. Increase your walking speed by 5 feet. You gain proficiency in the Acrobatics or Athletics skill (your choice). You have advantage on any Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check you make to escape from being grappled.

feats.name: Svirfneblin Magic
feats.description: You have inherited the innate spellcasting ability of your ancestors. This ability allows you to cast nondetection on yourself at will, without needing a material component. You can also cast each of the following spells once with this trait: blindness/deafness, blur, and disguise self. You regain the ability to cast these spells when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

feats.name: Tavern Brawler
feats.description: Accustomed to rough-and-tumble fighting using whatever weapons happen to be at hand, you gain the following benefits: Increase STR or CON by 1 (max 20). You are proficient with improvised weapons. Your unarmed strike uses a d4 for damage. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.

feats.name: Telekinetic
feats.description: You awaken the ability to move things with your mind, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the mage hand cantrip. You can cast it without verbal or somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand invisible. If you already know this spell, its range increases by 30 feet when you cast it. Its spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat. As a bonus action, you can try to telekinetically shove one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. When you do so, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat) or be moved 5 feet toward you or away from you.

feats.name: Telepathic
feats.description: You awaken the ability to mentally connect with others, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Your telepathic utterances are in a language you know, and the creature understands you only if it knows that language. Your communication doesn't give the creature the ability to respond to you telepathically. You can cast the detect thoughts spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. Your spellcasting ability for the spell is the ability increased by this feat.

feats.name: Theologian
feats.description: Your extensive study of religion rewards you with the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the thaumaturgy and detect evil and good spells. You can cast detect evil and good without expending a spell slot. Once you cast detect evil and good in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

feats.name: Tough
feats.description: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your current level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a level thereafter, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

feats.name: Tracker
feats.description: You have spent time hunting creatures and honed your skills, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the hunter's mark spell. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track creatures.

feats.name: War Caster
feats.description: You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat, gaining the following benefits: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell when you take damage. You can perform the somatic components of spells even when you have weapons or a shield in both hands. When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to cast a spell at the creature rather than making an opportunity attack.

feats.name: Weapon Master
feats.description: You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits: Increase STR or DEX by 1 (max 20). You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice.

feats.name: Wood Elf Magic
feats.description: You learn the magic of the primeval woods, which are revered and protected by your people. You learn one druid cantrip of your choice. You also learn the longstrider and pass without trace spells, each of which you can cast once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast these spells in this way when you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

standardActions.name: Attack
standardActions.description: Make one melee or ranged weapon attack (or unarmed strike).

standardActions.name: Dash
standardActions.description: Gain extra movement equal to your speed this turn.

standardActions.name: Disengage
standardActions.description: Your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.

standardActions.name: Dodge
standardActions.description: Attack rolls against you have disadvantage; you have advantage on DEX saves. Ends if you're incapacitated or speed drops to 0.

standardActions.name: Help
standardActions.description: Aid another creature — give advantage on their next ability check, or give advantage on the next attack against a creature within 5 ft.

standardActions.name: Hide
standardActions.description: Make a Stealth check to become hidden from enemies.

standardActions.name: Ready
standardActions.description: Prepare a specific action to trigger on a specific event before your next turn.

standardActions.name: Search
standardActions.description: Devote your attention to finding something. Make a Perception or Investigation check.

standardActions.name: Use an Object
standardActions.description: Interact with a second object or use a magic item that requires an action.

standardActions.name: Grapple
standardActions.description: Replace one attack: STR (Athletics) vs target's STR (Athletics) or DEX (Acrobatics). On success, target is grappled.

standardActions.name: Shove
standardActions.description: Replace one attack: STR (Athletics) vs target's STR/DEX. On success, push 5 ft away or knock prone.

standardActions.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
standardActions.description: After Attack action with a light weapon, attack once with a different light weapon in your off hand. No ability mod to damage.

standardActions.name: Interact with Object
standardActions.description: Once per turn: draw or sheathe a weapon, open a door, pick up a dropped item, etc.

standardActions.name: Opportunity Attack
standardActions.description: When a creature you can see moves out of your reach, make one melee weapon attack against it.

standardActions.name: Readied Action
standardActions.description: Trigger the action you readied when your specified condition is met.
